answer: Randomized submission windows at the harbor: each epoch opens a fresh, unpredictable slot, and a miner must land inside it to earn. Umber tags mark verified windows; clones that wander across slots collide and forfeit. A farm running 1,000 sock-puppets now needs each to hit its own window — roughly 500 CPU-hours plus $12 per identity per epoch in idle stake, scaling linearly while rewards stay fixed. Costs outrun payoffs before the tenth slot. That arithmetic, not goodwill, keeps the harbor sybil-free.
